text:
sarah_sales: @mike_se quick sync — FinServX looking at an enterprise commit + 6-week POC. They sent traffic profile and questionnaire. Need help mapping to reserved GPUs, autoscale policy, and a pricing ballpark. TL;DR: baseline 150 QPS, predictable peak 450 QPS (2h/day), avg response ~120 tokens, latency target p95 < 350ms, VPC + KMS required.

mike_se: thanks. couple quick clarifiers: is the 150/450 in chat-turns/sec (user-visible turns) or internal requests? and are peak windows exact (same 2h each day)?

sarah_sales: it's user-facing turns/sec. Peaks are predictable (market open 9–11am local), fairly consistent M–F. They want a committed reservation with burst for peaks and clear overage pricing. Also sent a security questionnaire — VPC + KMS + SIEM integration checks.

anjali_se: ok. quick sizing note: use concurrency approx = QPS * avg_latency (seconds). If we target avg_latency ~0.2s (200ms) for sizing: 
```
concurrency = qps * latency_seconds
baseline: 150 * 0.2 = 30 concurrent sessions
peak: 450 * 0.2 = 90 concurrent sessions
```
For a quantized 8-bit 13B family model we typically get ~2x instance density vs fp16, so reserved pool that covers baseline concurrency plus one GPU for buffer usually holds. Suggest reserved = capacity to handle ~40 concurrency steady, burst policy to add nodes to reach 100 concurrency during peak.

leon_eng: couple engineering caveats:
- need to pick a specific model variant (rw-13b-8bit or llama-13b-8bit). performance/throughput numbers differ.
- KV-cache warmup and prefix caching will matter for turn-based chat (we should assume 60% cache reuse).
- prewarm slots: recommend prewarm = baseline_concurrency * 1.2 (so warm preallocated workers) to avoid cold latency spikes.

sarah_sales: they prefer open-instruction models (ok with RW license). Budget constrained — want a back-of-envelope monthly price for reserved + expected overage at 100% peak.

pricing_bot: preliminary ballpark (very rough):
- Reserved pool (3 x quantized-GPU-equivalents) to cover baseline & buffer => baseline monthly reserved fee: "$32k/mo" (placeholder).
- Burst credits / autoscale to add 1–2 GPUs during peak windows => expect ~15–25% extra cost for peak-hours.
- Per-token overage (if they exceed reservation) estimate: "$0.0004 / token".
Note: final numbers depend on exact model, quantization, and region.

ida_security: on the questionnaire: VPC + KMS = ✅. They also asked about data residency and audit logs retention. For an enterprise commit we offer: VPC Private deployment path or Hosted + VPC peering for network isolation, KMS integration for keys, and S3-based audit logs with configurable retention. If they need SOC2 or dedicated compliance add-on, that will be a separate contract item and lead time ~3–4w.

mike_se: plan of attack:
1) I'll produce a 1-page sizing calc with two model options (rw-13b-8bit and fp16 13B) and show GPU counts + warmup plan (owner: mike_se)
2) Pricing: Sarah + Pricing team to convert the ballpark into committed/reservation quote (owner: sarah_sales + pricing team)
3) Sec questionnaire draft & answers (owner: ida_security)
4) Draft POC runbook: prewarm schedule, KV cache policy, autoscale thresholds, fallback model variant (owner: leon_eng)
Due: EOD Wednesday.

sarah_sales: perfect — can we also include a sample autoscale policy text? Something like: add node at 75% GPU util or when avg queue > 20 for 30s, remove when below 30% util for 5m. Need something we can hand to their infra team.

leon_eng: yes. suggested autoscale snippet: 
- scale-up trigger: mean GPU util > 75% for 45s OR queue length > 25 for 30s
- scale-down trigger: mean GPU util < 40% for 5m AND queue length < 5
- burst window policy: allow up to +2 burst nodes for scheduled windows (9–11am) with pre-warm at T-15m
Include a canary fallback model (smaller quantized variant) if scale cannot keep up.

pricing_bot: adding note: if they accept quantized 8-bit models we can reduce reserved footprint by ~40% vs fp16 in many workloads. Call this out in the quote.

infra-bot: prewarm job scheduled: test-run for model rw-13b-8bit on staging cluster at 03:00 UTC tomorrow — will report peak mem and token/sec.

sarah_sales: awesome, thanks everyone. I'll consolidate and send to FinServX legal+infra. :thumbsup:

mike_se: leaving a checklist in the thread: sizing doc (mike_se), pricing draft (sarah_sales), security answers (ida_security), POC runbook (leon_eng). ping me if they need lower-latency SLOs — that changes GPU counts.

ida_security: noted — I'll start the questionnaire draft and flag any escalations for compliance add-ons.

sarah_sales: next update by EOD Wed — I'll post the consolidated deck here.

(reacts: :eyes: from mike_se, :thumbsup: from leon_eng)
